messages.subject: Pushed support for unit_vector type
parts:
I just pushed support for a new unit_vector type.  I've added unit tests and information in the manual.

I didn't have a real Stan use-case for it, but I had needed to work out all the necessary math for another project recently and figured I might as well add it to Stan.

At any rate, you can now put:

unit_vector[N] dir_vector;

and get a vector with norm of 1.

This uses hyperspherical coordinates and so will suffer from singularities at certain points.  This shouldn't cause a big problem in practice unless people are unlucky.  However, it is theoretically possible and, because of the Jacobian term, certain vectors (namely 1,0,...,0 up to 0,...,0,1,0) cannot be used as an initialization because they are exactly at a singularity.

Let me know if anything crops up.

Cheers,
Marcus

On Thu, Mar 7, 2013 at 6:20 PM, Marcus Brubaker <marcus.a...@gmail.com> wrote:

I just pushed support for a new unit_vector type.  I've added unit tests and information in the manual.

I didn't have a real Stan use-case for it, but I had needed to work out all the necessary math for another project recently and figured I might as well add it to Stan.

At any rate, you can now put:

unit_vector[N] dir_vector;

and get a vector with norm of 1.

This uses hyperspherical coordinates and so will suffer from singularities at certain points.  This shouldn't cause a big problem in practice unless people are unlucky.  However, it is theoretically possible and, because of the Jacobian term, certain vectors (namely 1,0,...,0 up to 0,...,0,1,0) cannot be used as an initialization because they are exactly at a singularity.

Let me know if anything crops up.

Cheers,
Marcus

On Thu, Mar 7, 2013 at 6:20 PM, Marcus Brubaker <marcus.a...@gmail.com> wrote:
I just pushed support for a new unit_vector type.  I've added unit tests and information in the manual.

I didn't have a real Stan use-case for it, but I had needed to work out all the necessary math for another project recently and figured I might as well add it to Stan.

At any rate, you can now put:

unit_vector[N] dir_vector;

and get a vector with norm of 1.

This uses hyperspherical coordinates and so will suffer from singularities at certain points.  This shouldn't cause a big problem in practice unless people are unlucky.  However, it is theoretically possible and, because of the Jacobian term, certain vectors (namely 1,0,...,0 up to 0,...,0,1,0) cannot be used as an initialization because they are exactly at a singularity.

Let me know if anything crops up.

Cheers,
Marcus
